newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa industrials rally at close but end down.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa industrials rally at close but end down.

text.p: South African shares took a battering on Thursday as New Year's cheer was replaced by a festive hangover on Wall Street, dealers said.
A Tuesday night 101 point drop in New York, spurred by interest rate fears, hit global markets across Asia and Europe. South African stocks did not escape the gloom.

The fall was accentuated by a reaction to window dressing towards the year-end as unit trusts sought to boost their books before the close of 1996. This left some shares overpriced and they took a tumble on 1997's first trading day.

The all-share index shed 40.6 points to 6,616.9 as the industrial index fell 62.1 points to 7,859.5. But the final scores were generally off the day's lows as industrials launched a late rally as some traders saw the market as becoming oversold.
They pointed out that underlying support looked strong for South African markets and the sector had weathered Thursday's storm better than most European bourses.
The gold index had a rough day as bullion prices started to slip. London gold was fixed at its lowest level since December 3, 1996, after a late sell-off in new York on Tuesday.
The golds index lost 1.2 percent, or 18.1 points, to end at 1,488.1.
